items.claim: This unit's boundary from the narration-onset at 36:1 through the delegation's arrival at 36:3 carries both its own seams from tier-1 narrative-frame signals.
items.evidence: The wayehi-plus-date-formula opening web:Isa.36.1, וַיְהִ֡י בְּאַרְבַּע֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה שָׁנָ֜ה (byte tier, oshb:Isa.36.1), begins the narrative zone's own first scene rather than continuing prior oracle material; oshb:Isa.35.10 carries a PE mark (tier-3, single-witness) that the row correctly treats as neighbor corroboration for the preceding oracle's own close rather than internal boundary evidence. The forward close at web:Isa.36.3 sits immediately before the Rabshakeh's own royal-messenger formula opens at web:Isa.36.4, one of the book's exactly four royal-messenger koh-amar sites (byte-verified against the frame census), a genuine frame-onset this narration-only unit does not itself carry.

items.claim: The taunt's bounds from 36:4 through 36:10 correctly hold under a single royal-messenger frame, closing where the officials themselves interrupt.
items.evidence: web:Isa.36.4's own formula is one of exactly four royal-messenger koh-amar sites in the book (byte-verified against the frame census; the remaining 44 sites are divine-frame), correctly distinguished from Yahweh's own speech-frame. The bare-adonai token at oshb:Isa.36.8, אֶת אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר (byte tier), is the courtly "my master, the king of Assyria" sense rather than the divine title the same consonants carry at the throne vision, a role-split argued from the same clause's own apposition. The row's own forward close at 36:10 is warranted: the officials' own interjected request opens web:Isa.36.11 with a genuine speaker change from the Rabshakeh to the three officials, a tier-1 addressee/scene shift the row's own unit does not cross.

items.claim: The 36:11-12 exchange is a defensible dialogic unit bounded by real speaker changes on both sides, and the row honestly discloses the frame-plus-speech-merge rival rather than a strawman.
items.evidence: web:Isa.36.11 opens with a genuine speaker change to the three officials, a scene-internal interjection distinct from the Rabshakeh's own surrounding monologues, and web:Isa.36.13 opens with a fresh narration sequence, וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְקוֹל גָּד֖וֹל (byte tier, oshb:Isa.36.13, "Rabshakeh stood, and called out with a loud voice"), marking a re-narrated action and addressee shift to the wall-crowd that independently supports the row's own forward close at 36:12. The doubled ketiv/qere note at oshb:Isa.36.12 (2 notes, tier-3 single-witness) is correctly and symmetrically disclosed against the inventory. The row's disclosed rejected alternative, folding the whole 36:4-20 complex into one royal-messenger unit under the frame-plus-speech default, is the genuine live rival named for narrative-zone cuts generally, not an invented strawman, and the row's own medium-confidence, frontier-flagged hold is proportionate to that real tension.

items.claim: The two internal royal-messenger restatements at 36:14 and 36:16 are correctly kept inside one unit because neither carries an addressee or scene shift of its own.
items.evidence: Both oshb:Isa.36.14 and oshb:Isa.36.16 (byte tier) restate the same Assyrian king's frame to the same wall audience introduced at 36:13, with no intervening speaker or addressee change of the kind that bounds the 36:11-12 exchange; treating each koh-amar restatement as its own unit would be the sub-unit atomizing the hybrid granularity rule guards against. The SAMEKH mark at oshb:Isa.36.16 (tier-3, single-witness) is correctly disclosed without being read as a structural break. The row's own close at 36:20/36:21 is warranted: the quoted speech ends and third-person narration resumes at web:Isa.36.21 with the king's own silence-command, a genuine frame-closure the row does not cross.

items.claim: The row's forward boundary misplaces 37:1 on the officials'-report side of the seam, when the stronger tier-1 signal opens Hezekiah's own extended response there instead.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.36.22's own subject is the three officials telling Hezekiah the Rabshakeh's words, ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י רַב שָׁקֵֽה (byte tier, "and they told him the words of Rabshakeh"); oshb:Isa.37.1 opens with a fresh wayehi-plus-explicit-subject clause, וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ (byte tier, "and it happened when King Hezekiah heard"), shifting the acting subject from the delegation to the king himself and opening his own tear-clothes-and-temple response, which continues without any further scene marker straight into his sending the same delegation on to Isaiah at web:Isa.37.2. The row's own device_notes claim of shared participants across 36:21-37:1 is not accurate at the subject level: the delegation reports in 36:21-22, but Hezekiah alone acts from 37:1 onward. The row's disclosed rejected alternative, folding 36:21-22 backward into the Rabshakeh speech, is not the serious rival; the stronger contested cut is whether 37:1 belongs with Hezekiah's own response arc, continuing through the embassy to Isaiah, rather than closing the officials' report, and the row does not engage that rival.

items.claim: Hezekiah's own royal-messenger formula at 37:3, a genuine third frame-owner distinct from both the Assyrian king's sites and Yahweh's, is correctly bounded through Isaiah's answering divine word at 37:6-7.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.37.3 (byte tier) is one of exactly four royal-messenger koh-amar sites in the book's frame census alongside 36:4, 36:14, and 36:16, correctly named as Hezekiah's own frame rather than blended with either the Assyrian king's or Yahweh's; oshb:Isa.37.6 (byte tier) is independently one of the 44 divine-frame sites, correctly distinguished. The unit's own opening at 37:2 and close at 37:7 track the single delegation-and-reply scene; the row's disclosed rejected alternative, a split at 37:5, is a real, non-strawman candidate correctly set aside as mid-scene repetition rather than closure.

items.claim: The scene shift to the Rabshakeh's own return and Sennacherib's letter is correctly bounded from 37:8 through 37:13, and the row's own exclusion of 37:10 from the koh-amar census checks out against the inventory.
items.evidence: web:Isa.37.8 opens a genuine new scene, a new subject at a new location, Libnah, after the prior unit's close at 37:7; the letter's own introduction at web:Isa.37.10 uses a plain command-to-speak construction and is independently absent from the book's 48-verse koh-amar list, confirming the row's own disclaimer against inflating that census. The unit's close at 37:13 sits immediately before the narrated reception of the letter opens a fresh scene at web:Isa.37.14, a genuine addressee/scene shift from quoted-letter content to Hezekiah's own narrated action.

items.claim: Hezekiah's narrated act of spreading the letter and his prayer's own content are correctly held together as one frame-plus-speech unit closing the cluster's own assigned range at 37:20.
items.evidence: web:Isa.37.14's narration, receiving, reading, and spreading the letter before Yahweh, and the prayer's own content at web:Isa.37.15-Isa.37.20 share one participant and no intervening addressee or scene marker of the kind that elsewhere in this cluster bounds a unit, contrast the genuine speaker changes at 36:11 and 36:13; the frame-plus-speech default applied here matches the same treatment the book gives a narrated prayer with its own introduction. The row does not cross into Isaiah's own answering oracle beyond the assigned range.
